current_law_statement: Sessions reviewed: 2024 (HB 1854 c. 11 § 14; HB 3779 c. 116 § 2 — neither touched the fee paragraph), 2025 (SB 535 c. 404 § 2, eff. 11/1/2025 — added to 51 O.S. § 24A.5(4) the advance-payment permission ($75 estimated-cost threshold OR outstanding fees from previous requests) and the excess-refund duty, and added paragraph 7 request-form/reasonable-specificity provisions), and 2026 (SB 2184 c. 217 §§ 72–73, emerg. eff. 5/6/2026). MUST-DO check completed: the enrolled SB 535 text (opened, oklegislature.gov) was compared clause-by-clause against the OSCN 2026 codified print of § 24A.5; the only difference SB 2184 § 72 introduced is in paragraph 3, substituting 'Service Oklahoma' for 'the Department of Public Safety' in the driving-records assembly proviso (merging the duplicate Laws 2024 HB 1854 c. 11 § 14 amendment, which SB 2184 § 73 repealed as a duplicate section). SB 2184 § 72 made NO change to the fee provisions of paragraph 4. Codified availability: OSCN 2026 official prints of §§ 24A.3, 24A.5, 24A.21 were supplied as source documents (Kevin, 2026-08-20) and read in full. Guidance-vs-law gap: the OAG July-2025 one-pager tracks the statute; the OAG Open Records Request page (July 2026) publishes an AGENCY-SPECIFIC fee schedule ($0.50 color, $0.15 digital, $55/$85 hourly, quarter-hour billing, $55 minimum search fee, flash drive actual cost + $5.00) that is NOT municipal authority and is in visible tension with the size-based 25-cent copy cap for color pages. Oklahoma has no administrative-rule layer delegating or holding municipal ORA fee figures; § 24A.5(4) holds all the numbers itself.

resolutions.unit: USD per page (records 8.5 x 14 in or smaller)
resolutions.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(4)
resolutions.source_language: Notwithstanding any state or local provision to the contrary, in no instance shall the record copying fee exceed twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page for records having the dimensions of eight and one-half (8 1/2) by fourteen (14) inches or smaller, or a maximum of One Dollar ($1.00) per copied page for a certified copy.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (OSCN 2026 print; last amended by Laws 2025 SB 535 c. 404 § 2, eff. 11/1/2025, merged by Laws 2026 SB 2184 c. 217 § 72; the cap language is unchanged by both)
resolutions.notes: Ceiling, not a fixed value: the underlying permission is 'may charge a fee only for recovery of the reasonable, direct costs' (OK-0016), so the operative city rate is min(direct cost, $0.25). 'Notwithstanding any state or local provision to the contrary' is an express override of local enactments — binds municipalities directly.

resolutions.unit: USD per page (records 8.5 x 14 in or smaller; cap is size-based, no color distinction)
resolutions.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(4)
resolutions.source_language: Notwithstanding any state or local provision to the contrary, in no instance shall the record copying fee exceed twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page for records having the dimensions of eight and one-half (8 1/2) by fourteen (14) inches or smaller, or a maximum of One Dollar ($1.00) per copied page for a certified copy.
resolutions.manual_verification: The statute's copy cap is size-based with no color carve-out, yet the OAG's own published fee schedule (oklahoma.gov Open Records Request page, modified July 2026) charges $0.50/page for color copies. That schedule is agency-specific and not municipal authority, but the divergence suggests an interpretive question about whether color copying can be charged above $0.25. Verify before generating a color rate above the cap for any OK city.
resolutions.notes: No separate statutory color rate exists; the size-based cap facially covers color pages 8.5x14 or smaller. Resolved as the same $0.25 ceiling with a flag.

resolutions.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(4)
resolutions.source_language: Otherwise, a public body may charge a fee only for recovery of the reasonable, direct costs of record copying, or mechanical reproduction.
resolutions.notes: The $0.25 cap applies only to pages 8.5 x 14 in or smaller; larger/oversized pages fall back to the 'reasonable, direct costs' standard with no numeric cap. Standard's verbatim term: 'reasonable, direct costs of record copying, or mechanical reproduction'.

resolutions.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(4)
resolutions.source_language: Otherwise, a public body may charge a fee only for recovery of the reasonable, direct costs of record copying, or mechanical reproduction.
resolutions.notes: No specialty schedule (photos, maps, transcripts) for municipalities in the ORA; the reasonable-direct-cost standard governs. Where another state statute prescribes a per-record cost for a specific record type, that prescribed cost may be assessed instead (OK-0024 branch).

resolutions.notes: No graduated per-page bands by volume anywhere in the ORA; the copy cap is a flat $0.25/page ceiling. A city may adopt tiers only beneath the ceiling and the direct-cost basis (OK-0016/OK-0017).

resolutions.source_authority: None found — searched 51 O.S. §§ 24A.1–24A.34 fee provisions (OSCN 2026 prints), 2024–2026 session laws, OAG guidance (July 2025 one-pager)

resolutions.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(4)
resolutions.source_language: However, if the request: a. is solely for commercial purpose, or b. would clearly cause excessive disruption of the essential functions of the public body, then the public body may charge a reasonable fee to recover the direct cost of record search and copying;
resolutions.notes: No hourly figure for municipalities. Search labor is chargeable ONLY in the two OK-0019 circumstances (see labor.billableWhen), and then only as 'a reasonable fee to recover the direct cost of record search and copying'. The OAG's own $55/$85 per hour rates are agency-specific illustration, not municipal authority.

resolutions.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(3)–(4)
resolutions.source_language: Any reasonably segregable portion of a record containing exempt material shall be provided after deletion of the exempt portions; […] Otherwise, a public body may charge a fee only for recovery of the reasonable, direct costs of record copying, or mechanical reproduction.
resolutions.manual_verification: Interpretive: § 24A.5(4)'s exclusive fee basis ('only for recovery of the reasonable, direct costs of record copying, or mechanical reproduction') leaves no category for review/redaction labor on standard municipal requests, and the segregation duty in § 24A.5(3) carries no fee authorization. However, the OAG's own agency schedule charges $55/$85 per hour for 'legal review / redaction', so the exclusive-basis reading is not universally followed in practice. Human review recommended before hard-blocking review charges.
resolutions.notes: Categorically non-chargeable for standard requests — a review/redaction hourly rate has no statutory home. For commercial/disruptive requests the permitted fee covers 'record search and copying' (OK-0019), which does not name review either. Source language joins § 24A.5(3) first sentence and the § 24A.5(4) exclusive-basis sentence; ellipsis marks the intervening text.

resolutions.source_authority: None found — searched 51 O.S. §§ 24A.1–24A.34 (OSCN 2026 prints), 2024–2026 session laws (SB 535, SB 2184 opened), OAG guidance
resolutions.notes: No programming/data-extraction fee provision. The exclusive fee basis (OK-0016) covers direct costs of copying/mechanical reproduction only, and there is no duty to create a new record (51 O.S. § 24A.18, per OAG one-pager) — so bespoke programming work is more naturally refused than billed. The only electronic-data fee text is the news-media direct-cost cap (OK-0020) and the DPS-specific sentence (state agency only).

resolutions.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(4)
resolutions.source_language: However, if the request: a. is solely for commercial purpose, or b. would clearly cause excessive disruption of the essential functions of the public body, then the public body may charge a reasonable fee to recover the direct cost of record search and copying; […] In no case shall a search fee be charged when the release of records is in the public interest, including, but not limited to, release to the news media, scholars, authors and taxpayers seeking to determine whether those entrusted with the affairs of the government are honestly, faithfully, and competently performing their duties as public servants.
resolutions.notes: Shape: labor (search) is billable ONLY when the request is (a) solely for a commercial purpose or (b) would clearly cause excessive disruption of essential functions; NEVER when release is in the public interest (mandatory override, OK-0022); news-media use is excluded from 'commercial' (OK-0020). No page or hour threshold, no paper-only scope. This is a classification gate the engine executes, not a value.

resolutions.source_language: A public body may require advance payment of the estimated fees authorized under this section when the estimated cost exceeds Seventy-five Dollars ($75.00) or if the requestor has outstanding fees from previous requests. Any portion of an advance payment that exceeds the costs of responding to the request shall be returned to the requestor.
resolutions.effective_status: Current — added by Laws 2025 SB 535, eff. 11/1/2025
resolutions.manual_verification: The 100% ceiling is an inference from the clause's object — the permission is to require advance payment 'of the estimated fees', i.e., up to the full estimate, with mandatory refund of any excess over actual cost. No express percent cap exists; confirm the full-estimate reading is acceptable to the generator (alternative: treat percent cap as silent).
resolutions.notes: No fractional deposit cap in Oklahoma; the advance payment may be the entire estimated fee. Any collected excess over the actual cost of responding must be returned (OK-9002).

resolutions.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(4), as amended by Laws 2025, SB 535, c. 404, § 2
resolutions.source_language: A public body may require advance payment of the estimated fees authorized under this section when the estimated cost exceeds Seventy-five Dollars ($75.00) or if the requestor has outstanding fees from previous requests.
resolutions.effective_status: Current — added by Laws 2025 SB 535, eff. 11/1/2025
resolutions.notes: Shape: production may be conditioned on payment only through the advance-payment gate, and only when one of its two triggers holds (estimate > $75, or outstanding prior fees). Outside those triggers the ORA gives no express authority to withhold records pending payment, and the prompt-reasonable-access duty of § 24A.5(6) limits delay to preparation time and disruption-avoidance.

resolutions.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(4), as amended by Laws 2025, SB 535, c. 404, § 2

resolutions.notes: The statutory nonpayment consequence is prior-debt prepayment: a requestor with outstanding fees from previous requests may be required to pay the new request's estimated fees in advance regardless of amount (OK-9003). The ORA is silent on a withdrawn-after-N-days rule and on any deemed-abandonment timeline for unpaid fees.

resolutions.notes: Oklahoma has no numeric production deadline to toll ('prompt, reasonable access' soft standard, § 24A.5(6)), and the SB 535 advance-payment clause says nothing about the effect of an unpaid advance payment on that duty, no grace period, and no lapse action. Whether awaiting a demanded advance payment is a permissible 'delay' under § 24A.5(6) is unaddressed.

No revised-estimate requirement when actuals exceed the estimate, no collection block, no window restart. The engine must execute the refund step on close-out when an advance payment was taken.

resolutions.source_language: Otherwise, a public body may charge a fee only for recovery of the reasonable, direct costs of record copying, or mechanical reproduction.
resolutions.notes: No CD/DVD/USB figure in the ORA; the medium's direct cost is recoverable under the copying/mechanical-reproduction basis (scope judgment: 'record copying' read to include the physical medium's direct cost). Electronic data for news media capped at direct cost of making the copy (OK-0020). OAG's 'Flash Drive: Actual Cost + $5.00' is agency-specific illustration only — the +$5 surcharge has no statutory basis for cities.

resolutions.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(4)
resolutions.source_language: Notwithstanding any state or local provision to the contrary, in no instance shall the record copying fee exceed twenty-five cents ($0.25) per page for records having the dimensions of eight and one-half (8 1/2) by fourteen (14) inches or smaller, or a maximum of One Dollar ($1.00) per copied page for a certified copy.
resolutions.notes: Certified-copy ceiling $1.00 per copied page; sits inside the same 'notwithstanding any state or local provision' clause, so it binds municipalities directly. Per-record statutory fees prescribed by other state law can displace it for specific record types (OK-0024).

resolutions.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(4); definitions at § 24A.3(1)
resolutions.source_language: Otherwise, a public body may charge a fee only for recovery of the reasonable, direct costs of record copying, or mechanical reproduction.
resolutions.notes: No per-recording, per-minute, or free-minutes figure anywhere in the ORA. Sound/film/video recordings are 'records' (§ 24A.3(1), OSCN 2026 print opened), so reproduction is chargeable only at reasonable direct cost; the per-page caps do not fit non-paper media. Law-enforcement audio/video access rules (§ 24A.8) contain no municipal fee figures.

resolutions.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(4)
resolutions.source_language: However, if the request: a. is solely for commercial purpose, or b. would clearly cause excessive disruption of the essential functions of the public body, then the public body may charge a reasonable fee to recover the direct cost of record search and copying; however, publication in a newspaper or broadcast by news media for news purposes shall not constitute a resale or use of a record for trade or commercial purpose and charges for providing copies of electronic data to the news media for a news purpose shall not exceed the direct cost of making the copy.
resolutions.notes: Shape, not a surcharge percentage: on a solely-commercial (or excessively disruptive) request, search labor becomes chargeable at 'a reasonable fee to recover the direct cost of record search and copying'. News-media news use is excluded from 'commercial' and its electronic-data charges capped at direct copy cost (OK-0020). No commercial rate multiplier exists.

resolutions.source_authority: Okla. Stat. tit. 51, § 24A.5(4)
resolutions.source_language: In no case shall a search fee be charged when the release of records is in the public interest, including, but not limited to, release to the news media, scholars, authors and taxpayers seeking to determine whether those entrusted with the affairs of the government are honestly, faithfully, and competently performing their duties as public servants. The fees shall not be used for the purpose of discouraging requests for information or as obstacles to disclosure of requested information;
resolutions.notes: Grounds: public-interest release (illustrative list: news media, scholars, authors, taxpayer-accountability requests). Mandatory ('In no case shall'), but scope is the SEARCH fee only — copy fees are not waived by statute. No purpose-statement requirement, no written-denial duty, and no waiver-specific appeal in the ORA (the Public Access Counselor, § 24A.40, is a general compliance-review channel). A narrow mandatory no-charge rule also exists for § 24A.5(3)-authorized fees when a state agency or taxing entity in a Local Development Act district requests LDA reports (§ 24A.21) — not a municipal-requester scenario the portal will see; noted for completeness.

resolutions.notes: No fee-forfeiture-on-late-response rule in Oklahoma (there is no numeric response deadline to be late against; access duty is 'prompt, reasonable'). Enforcement runs through § 24A.17 remedies, not fee forfeiture.

resolutions.notes: Oklahoma's only cross-request rule is the prior-debt gate (OK-9003): outstanding fees from previous requests authorize demanding advance payment on any new request, which requires a per-requestor debt ledger. No aggregation threshold, no request-combining rule, no carry-forward regime. The 'excessive disruption' prong (OK-0019) can also be triggered by request volume but states no aggregation mechanics.

applicability_notes: § 24A.3(2) 'public body' expressly includes 'county, city, village, town, township, district, school district' — every § 24A.5(4) fee rule binds municipalities unless its own text narrows it (OSCN 2026 print of § 24A.3 opened).

The 25-cent copy cap and $1.00 certified-copy cap open with 'Notwithstanding any state or local provision to the contrary' — an express preemption of local enactments; a city ordinance cannot set a higher standard-page rate.

The sentence 'The fee charged by the Department of Public Safety for a copy in a computerized format of a record of the Department shall not exceed the direct cost of making the copy unless the fee for the record is otherwise set by law' is state_agencies_only (DPS-specific); it resolves nothing for municipalities and was not attached to any item.

The OAG fee schedule on the oklahoma.gov Open Records Request page (color $0.50, digital $0.15, $55/$85 hourly, quarter-hour increments, $55 minimum search fee, flash drive actual cost + $5.00, opinion-book prices, sales tax note) is the Attorney General's own agency schedule under § 24A.5(7)/(4) — agency-specific illustration, never municipal authority. Its hourly and minimum figures were deliberately NOT used to resolve any municipal item.

§ 24A.21 bars charging § 24A.5-authorized fees when a state agency or taxing entity within a Local Development Act district requests the LDA-required reports — a real municipal no-charge rule but for government requesters of one report type; noted in the waiver row rather than emitted as a checklist value.

Oklahoma has no administrative-rule layer for ORA fees: § 24A.5(4) contains no delegation to any rulemaking body, and each public body sets its own posted schedule (OK-0021). The only outward reference — 'cost … otherwise prescribed by state law' (OK-0024) — points to record-type-specific statutes (e.g., 47 O.S. § 6-117 DPS records), not to a fee-schedule instrument holding municipal numbers; there was therefore no delegated instrument to open.
material_negatives: No municipal labor-rate figure of any kind (search, review, programming) — search labor is gated to commercial/disruptive requests and then priced only by the reasonable-direct-cost standard; review/redaction labor has no fee authorization at all.
No estimate apparatus: no itemized-estimate/cost-notice threshold, no requester response window, no revision-at-N% rule, no estimate validity period.
No deposit percent cap smaller than the full estimate; no clock/grace/lapse rules for an unpaid advance payment (Oklahoma has no numeric production clock to toll).
No de-minimis threshold, no minimum fee, no free-page or free-labor-hour allowances, no graduated page bands.
No delivery/postage, electronic-media, or audio/video fee figures; all fall back to the reasonable-direct-cost basis or are simply unaddressed.
No fee-forfeiture-on-late-response rule; no withdrawal-after-N-days nonpayment rule (the only nonpayment consequence is the prior-debt advance-payment gate, OK-9003).
No administrative-rule or uniform-fee-schedule layer for ORA fees anywhere in Oklahoma law — every figure the state sets lives directly in 51 O.S. § 24A.5(4).

Absence statements rest on full reads of the supplied OSCN 2026 prints (§§ 24A.3, 24A.5, 24A.21), the enrolled 2025 SB 535, the 2026 SB 2184 duplicate-section merger, and the OAG July-2025 one-pager; absence of a found rule is not proof none exists elsewhere in uncompiled law.
